listening.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
listening.topic: El Niño is suppressing Atlantic hurricane activity in 2026, potentially making it the first hurricane-free season in the satellite era.
listening.topic_zh: 2026年聖嬰現象正在抑制大西洋颶風活動，可能使其成為衛星時代以來首個無颶風的季節。
listening.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to 6 Minute English. Today we're looking at one of the most fascinating meteorological stories of 2026 — the near-complete absence of Atlantic hurricanes during what is traditionally the most dangerous time of year. September is normally the peak month for hurricane activity in the Atlantic, yet this year, not a single hurricane has formed. So what is going on? The answer lies thousands of kilometres away in the Pacific Ocean, where a powerful climate phenomenon known as El Niño is reshaping weather patterns across the globe. El Niño refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific. This warming sets off a chain reaction in atmospheric circulation, increasing wind shear over the Atlantic — essentially strong winds at different altitudes that tear apart the organised storm systems needed for hurricanes to develop. While the Atlantic sits quietly, the eastern North Pacific has been extraordinarily active this season, with above-average storm activity — a classic signature of El Niño conditions. Forecasters at both the US National Hurricane Center and Colorado State University had anticipated a below-normal Atlantic season, predicting between eight and fourteen named storms in total, with only one to three becoming major hurricanes. So far, that prediction is proving remarkably accurate. If no hurricane forms before the season officially ends, 2026 will go down in history as a truly extraordinary year for Atlantic weather.

vocabulary.definition: to suppress or prevent something from developing or continuing, especially a natural process
vocabulary.definition_zh: 壓制、抑制某事物的發展或持續
vocabulary.example: El Niño tends to stifle hurricane formation in the Atlantic by increasing wind shear across the basin.

vocabulary.definition: a difference in wind speed or direction at different altitudes in the atmosphere, which disrupts the development of tropical storms
vocabulary.definition_zh: 風切變，指大氣不同高度之間風速或風向的差異，會阻礙熱帶風暴的發展
vocabulary.example: High levels of wind shear over the Atlantic this season have prevented tropical disturbances from intensifying into hurricanes.

vocabulary.definition: relating to the science of weather and atmospheric conditions
vocabulary.definition_zh: 氣象學的，與天氣及大氣條件科學相關的
vocabulary.example: Meteorological agencies around the world closely monitor El Niño events because of their far-reaching impacts.

vocabulary.definition: the period from the 1960s onwards during which weather satellites have provided continuous global monitoring of atmospheric and oceanic conditions
vocabulary.definition_zh: 衛星時代，指自1960年代起氣象衛星持續提供全球大氣和海洋監測的時期
vocabulary.example: Records show that the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is unprecedented within the satellite era.

vocabulary.definition: to interrupt or interfere with the normal course of a process or system, causing it to function abnormally
vocabulary.definition_zh: 打亂、干擾正常過程或系統的運作
vocabulary.example: Strong El Niño conditions are expected to disrupt wind patterns across the Atlantic for the remainder of the season.

questions.q: According to the episode, what is the PRIMARY reason why no hurricanes have formed in the Atlantic this season?
options: A: Unusually cold Atlantic sea surface temperatures
B: The influence of the El Niño climate phenomenon
C: A reduction in the number of tropical depressions
D: Accurate storm forecasting by meteorological agencies
questions.explanation: The episode explicitly states that El Niño is the biggest reason for the suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity, as it increases wind shear over the Atlantic, preventing storm development.

questions.q: How many named tropical storms formed in the Atlantic during September of this season?
questions.explanation: The episode mentions four named tropical storms in September: Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo, and Hanna — though none of them reached hurricane strength.

questions.q: Which institution predicted between eight and fourteen named storms for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season?
options: C: The US National Hurricane Center
D: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
questions.explanation: The episode states that the US National Hurricane Center, in May, predicted a total of eight to fourteen named storms for the season, based on the strong El Niño forecast.

reading.title: El Niño and the Suppression of Atlantic Hurricane Activity
reading.passage:
The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has attracted global scientific attention due to a remarkable meteorological anomaly: the complete absence of hurricane formation throughout September, historically the most active month of the season. This phenomenon is largely attributed to the powerful El Niño event currently influencing global climate systems.

El Niño is characterised by the anomalous warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. This warming fundamentally alters large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns. Of particular significance for Atlantic hurricane activity is the substantial increase in vertical wind shear — the variation in wind speed and direction across different atmospheric levels — that El Niño generates over the Atlantic basin. Organised tropical convection, which is essential for hurricane development, is effectively dismantled by these opposing wind forces before a coherent storm system can establish itself.

The inverse relationship between El Niño and Atlantic hurricane activity is well documented. During strong El Niño events, the eastern North Pacific experiences significantly elevated storm activity, while the Atlantic simultaneously endures a suppressed season. This contrast was clearly evident in 2026, as the eastern North Pacific recorded above-average tropical cyclone frequency while the Atlantic remained largely dormant.

Prior to the season, forecasters at the US National Hurricane Center projected eight to fourteen named storms, with one to three reaching major hurricane intensity — a notably conservative estimate compared to recent seasons. Colorado State University's meteorological team corroborated these projections, citing the El Niño-driven disruption of Atlantic wind patterns as a key suppressing factor.

Should the Atlantic season conclude without a single hurricane, 2026 would represent a singular event in the recorded history of tropical meteorology. Since continuous satellite monitoring began in the 1960s, no Atlantic hurricane season has been entirely devoid of at least one hurricane. Scientists caution, however, that such anomalies, while rare, are consistent with the known variability of El Niño's influence on global weather systems.

questions.statement: El Niño increases wind shear over the Atlantic Ocean, which helps tropical storms develop into hurricanes.
questions.explanation: The passage states that El Niño generates substantial wind shear over the Atlantic, which dismantles organised tropical convection and PREVENTS hurricane development, not helps it.

questions.statement: The eastern North Pacific Ocean experienced above-average tropical storm activity during the same period that the Atlantic remained quiet.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the eastern North Pacific recorded above-average tropical cyclone frequency while the Atlantic remained largely dormant — a classic El Niño pattern.

questions.statement: Colorado State University expressed doubt about whether El Niño was truly responsible for the suppressed Atlantic hurricane season.
questions.explanation: The passage states that Colorado State University corroborated projections of a below-normal season, citing El Niño-driven disruption as a key factor — indicating support, not doubt.

questions.q: What would make the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season historically significant, according to the passage?
options: A: It would be the season with the fewest named tropical storms on record
B: It would be the first Atlantic hurricane season without a single hurricane in the satellite era
C: It would mark the strongest El Niño event ever recorded in the Pacific
D: It would represent the most accurate seasonal hurricane forecast in history
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that if no hurricane forms, 2026 would be the first Atlantic hurricane season entirely devoid of a hurricane since continuous satellite monitoring began in the 1960s.

speaking.topic: Describe a time when extreme or unusual weather affected your daily life or plans.
speaking.topic_zh: 描述一次極端或異常天氣影響你日常生活或計劃的經歷。

part2.cue_card:
Describe a time when extreme or unusual weather affected your daily life or plans.

You should say:
• what the weather event was and when it happened
• how it affected your daily routine or specific plans
• how you and the people around you responded to the situation

And explain how this experience changed your attitude towards weather or climate issues.
band_tips: Use precise meteorological vocabulary where natural, such as 'unprecedented rainfall', 'atmospheric conditions', or 'severe disruption', to demonstrate lexical range and impress the examiner.

Organise your response with a clear narrative arc — set the scene, describe the impact, discuss the response, and finish with a reflective point about climate change or personal growth to show coherent discourse management.

Use a range of complex grammatical structures, including conditionals ('Had the storm arrived earlier, the damage would have been far worse'), perfect aspects, and passive constructions, to achieve a Band 8+ grammatical range score.

part3.q: Do you think governments are doing enough to prepare citizens for extreme weather events?
part3.q_zh: 你認為政府在為公民應對極端天氣事件方面做得足夠嗎？
key_points: Many governments invest in early warning systems and infrastructure reinforcement, but preparedness is often unequal between developed and developing nations.
Public education campaigns about disaster readiness remain insufficient in many countries, leaving vulnerable populations particularly exposed.
Climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of extreme weather, meaning current preparedness levels may be inadequate for future conditions.

part3.q: How do you think climate change is influencing global weather patterns?
part3.q_zh: 你認為氣候變化如何影響全球天氣模式？
key_points: Rising global temperatures are intensifying the water cycle, leading to more extreme precipitation events such as floods and droughts occurring simultaneously in different regions.
Climate change is altering the behaviour of established weather phenomena like El Niño, potentially making their effects more unpredictable and severe.
Scientists observe a clear trend of increasing frequency of Category 4 and 5 hurricanes, though the total number of tropical storms may not necessarily rise.

part3.q: Should individuals change their lifestyle to help reduce the impact of climate-related weather events?
part3.q_zh: 個人是否應該改變生活方式以幫助減少氣候相關天氣事件的影響？
key_points: Individual actions such as reducing carbon footprints through dietary choices and sustainable transport collectively contribute to mitigating long-term climate change.
However, systemic change through corporate regulation and government policy is likely to have a far greater impact than individual behavioural shifts alone.
There is an important psychological dimension — when individuals engage in sustainable behaviour, they become more politically active advocates for broader climate policy reform.

part3.q: How important is international cooperation in responding to global weather phenomena like El Niño?
part3.q_zh: 國際合作在應對聖嬰現象等全球天氣現象方面有多重要？
key_points: El Niño affects every continent and requires coordinated data sharing between meteorological agencies across nations to enable accurate forecasting and timely warnings.
International financial mechanisms, such as climate adaptation funds, allow wealthier nations to support vulnerable countries in building resilience against El Niño-related disasters.
Without multilateral agreements on greenhouse gas emissions, the underlying climate trends that may be intensifying El Niño events cannot be effectively addressed.

writing.task2_question: Some people believe that natural disasters such as hurricanes and floods are becoming more frequent and severe due to human activity, while others argue that these are simply natural cycles that have always occurred. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
writing.task2_question_zh: 一些人認為颶風和洪水等自然災害因人類活動而變得更加頻繁和嚴重，而另一些人認為這些只是一直存在的自然週期。討論兩種觀點並給出你自己的意見。

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use at the start of a body paragraph to introduce a widely accepted fact or premise before building your argument
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於段落開頭，引出廣為接受的事實或前提，再展開論點
useful_phrases.example: It is widely acknowledged that El Niño events have always influenced global weather patterns, independent of human activity.

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use to introduce a counterargument or contrasting scientific finding that challenges the preceding point
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於引入反駁論點或與前述觀點形成對比的科學發現
useful_phrases.example: However, compelling evidence suggests that rising ocean temperatures linked to carbon emissions are amplifying the destructive power of these natural phenomena.

useful_phrases.phrase: The consequences of ... extend far beyond
useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use to emphasise the wide-ranging or long-term impacts of a phenomenon, strengthening your argument about severity
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於強調某現象廣泛或長遠的影響，加強你對嚴重性的論點
useful_phrases.example: The consequences of increasingly intense hurricane seasons extend far beyond immediate property damage, affecting food security and public health for years afterwards.

useful_phrases.phrase: While it is true that ... , it would be an oversimplification to suggest that
useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use to concede a point from the opposing view while refuting an extreme version of that argument, demonstrating balanced critical thinking
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於承認對方觀點的同時反駁其極端版本，展現平衡的批判性思維
useful_phrases.example: While it is true that natural climate cycles like El Niño have always existed, it would be an oversimplification to suggest that human activity plays no role in their growing intensity.

useful_phrases.phrase: On balance, the weight of scientific evidence points to
useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use in the conclusion or final body paragraph to deliver your synthesised opinion based on the evidence discussed
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於結論或最後一個主體段落，根據前述討論的證據表達你的綜合觀點
useful_phrases.example: On balance, the weight of scientific evidence points to a clear human contribution to the increasing severity of extreme weather events globally.

outline.intro: Begin by contextualising the debate with a relevant observation — for instance, the unprecedented 2026 Atlantic hurricane season and the role of El Niño — to show topic awareness. Paraphrase the question and clearly state that the essay will discuss both perspectives before presenting a qualified opinion favouring the human-activity argument.
outline.body1: Present the 'natural cycles' viewpoint fairly and in detail. Explain that phenomena such as El Niño, volcanic activity, and Milankovitch orbital cycles have driven climate variability for millennia. Acknowledge that the 2026 quiet Atlantic season demonstrates how natural forces can suppress, as well as intensify, storm activity. Use hedging language to represent this view accurately without endorsing it fully.
outline.body2: Argue that anthropogenic climate change is amplifying natural weather variability beyond historical norms. Cite the scientific consensus that rising sea surface temperatures — driven by greenhouse gas emissions — intensify tropical cyclones when they do form, and that the frequency of the most destructive storms is increasing. Distinguish between total storm count and storm intensity to add analytical nuance.
outline.conclusion: Synthesise both views by acknowledging that natural cycles form the baseline of weather variability, but that human activity is increasingly distorting that baseline in dangerous ways. Restate your opinion clearly and end with a forward-looking statement about the urgency of international climate policy, leaving the examiner with a strong final impression.
